original_question: Given an infinite-dimensional Banach space X, what is the greatest possible order type of a Schauder basis carried by a quotient of X? In particular, must every non-separable Banach space have an uncountable biorthogonal system?
target_in_paper: Section 11, Problem 16 ('Quotients with long Schauder bases and biorthogonal systems'), together with the immediately following sentence noting that this asks in particular whether every non-separable Banach space has an uncountable biorthogonal system.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the exact topic of Section 11: the quotient version of the basis problem, namely how long a Schauder basis a quotient of an infinite-dimensional Banach space can have. It also correctly captures the paper’s immediate nearby consequence/question about uncountable biorthogonal systems in non-separable Banach spaces.
missing_details: The paper’s official numbered target is Problem 16; the biorthogonal-system clause is not itself the numbered problem there, but the immediate 'in particular' consequence stated right after Problem 16.

The paper says 'what is the longest Schauder basis a quotient of X can have?' rather than 'greatest possible order type,' which can suggest existence of a maximum; the official wording is deliberately less committal.
To be self-contained, the quotient should be specified as a Banach-space quotient X/Y by a closed subspace Y of X.
To make 'long' precise, one should say that the basis may be transfinite and that 'length' refers to the ordinal length/order type of a Schauder basis.

The draft does not define 'biorthogonal system'; the paper uses the standard Banach-space meaning, so the stand-alone question should spell out that this means a family {(x_i,f_i)} in X×X* with f_i(x_j)=δ_{ij}.

The paper imposes no extra hypotheses on X in Problem 16 beyond infinite dimensionality; the refined question should likewise avoid adding separability, reflexivity, Asplundness, or duality assumptions.
The paper does not add any special scalar-field restriction beyond standard Banach-space conventions, so the refined question should not introduce one.

If one wants the paper’s later set-theoretic sharpening, that is separated out as Problem 17 under PID; your draft does not mention that this is only a nearby reformulation, not the main official statement.
refined_question: Let X be an infinite-dimensional Banach space, and let Y range over the closed subspaces of X. What is the longest ordinal length of a transfinite Schauder basis that can occur in a Banach-space quotient X/Y? In particular, must every non-separable Banach space X admit an uncountable biorthogonal system, that is, an uncountable family {(x_i,f_i)}_{i∈I}⊂X×X* such that f_i(x_j)=δ_{ij} for all i,j∈I?
justification: The draft clearly points to Section 11 rather than to the earlier problems: Problem 16 is stated there verbatim as 'Given an infinite-dimensional Banach space X, what is the longest Schauder basis a quotient of X can have?' and the very next sentence says that this 'in particular asks if every non-separable Banach space has an uncountable biorthogonal system.' Section 10 supplies the immediate parent problem: Problem 16 is introduced as a natural variant of Problem 14, the classical quotient-with-a-basis problem. The same Section 11 then records the relevant nearby context showing why the second clause matters and why set theory enters: Theorem 16 gives a consistency obstruction, Theorem 17 and Corollary 18 give PID-based positive results, and Problem 17 isolates a narrower PID-specific reformulation. Since your draft asks for the general Banach-space problem, the paper-faithful refinement should stay centered on Problem 16 and keep the biorthogonal-system sentence only as the paper’s explicit 'in particular' corollary/question.
